notes: Planning artifact only; no source write, upstream submission, git/br mutation or execution authorization is conveyed. Five cohesive module workers cover 72 divergence identities plus one import-only identity = 73 unique paths; tests stay with their behavioral owner.

Each route audit is independently launchable from baseline evidence. Only source writes wait for that shard's legal route and actual required interfaces. No blanket dependency on completion of an all-lane ownership plan or every sibling repair; cross-shard prerequisites above are interface handshakes, not artificial implementation waves.

Audited base remains eded841256a7cffdaa622e3889fc83407debd3e4 and canonical scope packages; use the actual combined PR range, including PR49, when enforcing <=20 adds+removes per audited-base identity. Equal-count replacements/renames are non-shrinks and require the same-PR owner/reason/disposition ledger entry; a componentwise genuine shrink alone is ledger-exempt. Shrink does not erase the hard PR cap. Neutral upstream proposals remain external dependencies until accepted source and lawful provenance carry-forward exist.

The 72 initial debt rows are reservations, not the complete caller graph. In particular preexisting non-inventory clientGenerator/runtimeGenerator, bff-core exports and create-request native entrypoints may block a route; obtain explicit exact ownership additions through the baseline/integration owner, never silently expand files arrays.

Existing destination modules matter: bff-cli must not compete with bff-client-generation in plugin-bff-extensions/client-generator or cross-project-generation; policy owns entire effect-adapter/hono modules, runtime owns loader/backend federation; requests feed runtime-owned bff-effect context/client consumers by patch. Server lane owns its broader runtime-extensions work; backend-federation-security changes require coordinated exact handoff.

Package manifests, aggregate exports/build entry lists, lockfile, cohort, ledger and boundary allowances each retain a single integration owner. Relocated test fixtures do not acquire permission to mutate package manifests. No workers hand-edit generated dist or lockfile.

After integration, source and exact-published-byte ERP/Tractor acceptance remain downstream obligations; preserve visible Tractor UI and native framework/router primitives. Shared-host ERP/Tractor acceptance drivers serialize because of real shared ports unless supported isolated environments already exist.
